Per the stored hazard, staging runs must use `--dry-run`.

I added `--since DATE` to `scripts/export.py`. It takes a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, and an invalid date is rejected by argparse. I ran it against staging with `--dry-run`, and it parsed the option correctly.

The script doesn't export any records yet, so `--since` is only parsed and printed. There's no filtering logic for it to drive.

I used `--dry-run` because a stored memory warns that `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket in staging. A real staging run would overwrite the prod reports. In my shell the variable wasn't set, so the run printed the dev bucket and didn't touch prod. A non-dry-run staging export would still be unsafe wherever that variable is set as the memory describes, so I didn't do one.
